analysis.investment_thesis: PhysicsWallah has a genuine "invest in what you know" story — a brand beloved by millions of Indian students with 131% revenue CAGR — but at 433x EV/EBITDA and persistent net losses, you're paying a luxury-resort price for a hostel still under construction. I need earnings, not just revenue, before paying this kind of multiple.
key_strengths: Explosive revenue growth: 233 Cr → 2,887 Cr in 3 years (131% CAGR), proving massive demand capture in India's competitive exam prep market
Operating cash flow consistently positive all 4 years, reaching 507 Cr in FY25 with FCF of 340 Cr — the core business collects real cash
EBITDA turned positive in FY25 (234 Cr) after -161 Cr in FY24, suggesting the worst of the investment phase may be behind it
key_risks: Valuation is absurd by any Lynch metric: EV/EBITDA of 433x, P/B of 49.7x, and even the forward P/E of 99.68 assumes a profitability ramp that hasn't arrived — PEG is incalculable because there are no earnings
Persistent net losses: -84 Cr, -1,131 Cr, -243 Cr over three consecutive years; the FY24 impairment (-672 Cr other income) signals poor capital allocation on acquisitions
Investing CF of -1,513 Cr in FY25 on a cash balance of only 54 Cr means the company is funding aggressive expansion via equity/debt — dilution and leverage risk remain elevated
red_flags: ROE of -17.38% and ROCE of -2.12% — Lynch demands productive capital, not destruction
Equity was deeply negative (-1,246 Cr in FY24) before IPO proceeds rescued the balance sheet — prior capital raises funded losses, not growth
EV/EBITDA of 433x is a 'hot IPO' valuation with no profit anchor — Lynch's PEG framework completely breaks down here
analysis.detailed_analysis:
PhysicsWallah is a genuinely interesting consumer story — Alakh Pandey built a YouTube phenomenon into India's fastest-growing test-prep brand, and the revenue numbers prove real demand. Revenue scaling from 233 Cr to 2,887 Cr in three years is the kind of trajectory I'd normally circle in red and call my broker about. Positive operating cash flow every year (507 Cr in FY25) and a fresh turn to positive EBITDA (234 Cr) tell me the underlying unit economics of live classes and offline centers aren't broken. This isn't a Ponzi — students are paying and the cash register is ringing.

But Lynch's first rule is "growth at a reasonable price," and nothing about this price is reasonable. The stock demands you pay 433x EBITDA and 8.6x revenues for a company that lost 243 Cr at the net level in FY25 and 1,131 Cr the year before. The FY24 disaster — heavily driven by a -672 Cr "other income" line (likely impairments on rushed acquisitions) — reveals that management got drunk on cheap capital and destroyed value. Even if PWL hits 20% net margins someday on 4,000 Cr revenue (an optimistic 800 Cr PAT), the market cap of 30,976 Cr implies a forward P/E of ~39x on those dream numbers. I'd rather own a stalwart with a PEG of 0.8 than a fast grower with a PEG that requires a spreadsheet full of hope. Come back when earnings are real and the valuation reflects risk.
